newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreign navies to visit HK, U.S. to sail in first.
newsitem.headline: Foreign navies to visit HK, U.S. to sail in first.

text.p: The flagship of the United States Seventh Fleet will sail into Hong Kong next Monday in the first port call by a foreign navy since China took over the territory on July 1, Chinese and U.S. sources said on Monday.
An official at China's foreign ministry branch office in Hong Kong said foreign warships would continue to visit Hong Kong under Chinese rule, but Beijing's permission was needed.

The 7th Fleet flagship, USS Blue Ridge, would be the first warship to arrive when it sails into the world's busiest port on August 4, a U.S. Consulate official said. The USS Guardian and Patriot would follow a day later.
The three warships are on a routine recreational visit.
The U.S. Navy made about 70 port calls a year in Hong Kong when it was under British rule. Washington and Beijing have an agreement allowing the visits to continue.
Under British rule, visits by foreign warships required London's approval but, at least for western navies, the rule became just a minor formality.
Hong Kong Security Bureau officials said the foreign ministry office in the ex-colony would handle applications for naval visits and the Hong Kong government would be consulted.
China has promised the territory of 6.4 million people virtual autonomy in all but foreign affairs and defence.
